children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--The ICE Futures canola market fell to its lowest levels in seven weeks as spillover from losses in Chicago soybeans and chart-based speculative selling weighed on prices.

November canola was down by 10.00 Canadian dollars at C$801.70 per metric ton on Thursday, marking its lowest settlement since Aug. 27. The contract fell below its 50-day moving average but managed to hold above psychological support at C$800 per ton.
Losses in Chicago soybeans accounted for some spillover selling pressure, with European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil also lower. Soyoil futures held near unchanged.
Seasonal harvest pressure remained a bearish influence, although anecdotal reports that yields and quality may not live up to earlier expectations provided some support.
The Manitoba canola harvest was 86% complete in the latest provincial report, while 89% of the  Saskatchewan canola was off the field as of Oct. 12.
There were 107,034 contracts traded on Thursday, which compares with Wednesday when 96,944 contracts changed hands. Spreading accounted for 78,086 of the contracts traded.
